questions.q: Why does a dangerous-capability task suite need tasks spanning a meaningful difficulty range, rather than just one fixed task?
options: Difficulty range is irrelevant as long as the suite has enough tasks
A suite with only easy tasks can't distinguish a model that is barely capable from one that is highly capable
Easier tasks are always more dangerous than harder ones
Difficulty range only matters for persuasion evaluations
questions.explain: A graded range of difficulty is what lets an evaluation tell apart models that represent very different real risk levels, rather than lumping them together.

questions.q: What is 'uplift' in the context of a dangerous-capability evaluation?
options: The raw percentage of tasks a model passes
How much more capable a model makes a person at a dangerous task compared to their baseline resources, like a search engine
The speed increase a model provides over human-only work on any task
The amount of compute used to run the evaluation
questions.explain: Uplift compares an assisted condition against a baseline condition, since a model that only repeats freely available information isn't adding real risk even if it technically passes a task.

questions.q: Why is human-in-the-loop scoring still necessary for frontier dangerous-capability evaluations?
options: Because automated grading is always faster and should be avoided for speed reasons alone
Because open-ended outputs like exploit code or synthesis guidance often require expert judgment to tell whether they actually achieve the dangerous outcome
Because human scorers are needed only to format the final report
Because models cannot generate any output without a human present
questions.explain: Automated grading can't reliably judge whether open-ended, real-world-consequential outputs actually work, so human experts evaluate against real success criteria.

questions.q: Why do dangerous-capability evaluations need their own containment and ethical safeguards?
options: Because running the evaluation deliberately elicits the exact dangerous behavior it exists to screen for, which itself carries risk if mishandled
Because evaluations are run exclusively by regulators and never by labs
Containment is only a concern for safety evaluations, not capability evaluations
Because evaluations always involve financial transactions that need auditing
questions.explain: Since the evaluation process involves drawing out genuinely dangerous capability, it requires controlled environments and restricted access so the test itself doesn't become a source of real-world harm.

questions.q: Why does evaluation contamination matter for task design, as described in this lesson?
options: It doesn't matter, since models can't memorize evaluation content
If task content and solutions leak into training data, a model can appear more capable than it really is through memorization rather than genuine ability
Contamination only affects persuasion evaluations
Contamination makes evaluations run faster
questions.explain: A model that has seen a task's solution in training can pass it without possessing the underlying capability, which is why task suites like METR's limit how much content is published in full.
